title: How to Use Voice to Text on iPhone (2026)
summary: How to use voice to text on iPhone: turn on Dictation, the commands that punctuate and edit, fixes for when it stops working, and when to upgrade.
body_markdown:
Your iPhone has had voice to text built in for years, and most people only ever use a fraction of it. Apple calls it Dictation. It works anywhere you can type, it runs on the phone in many languages, and it understands spoken commands for punctuation, line breaks, and simple edits. This guide covers all of it, from turning it on to fixing it when the microphone key disappears, and what to try when the built-in tool is not enough.


**The short answer:** to use voice to text on iPhone, open **Settings** , tap **General** , then **Keyboard** , and turn on **Enable Dictation** . Then tap into any text field, tap the microphone on the keyboard, and speak. Say "period" or "new paragraph" for punctuation and line breaks, and tap the microphone again or say "Stop dictation" to finish.


## How to turn on voice to text on iPhone


Dictation is a keyboard setting. According to Apple's iPhone User Guide for iOS 27:


1. Open the **Settings** app.
2. Tap **General** , then tap **Keyboard** .
3. Turn on **Enable Dictation** . If a prompt appears, tap **Enable Dictation** again to confirm.


Below the switch, **About Dictation & Privacy** explains what Apple does with your audio. Apple says Dictation is processed on the iPhone in many languages with no internet connection required. One exception worth knowing: when you dictate into a search field, the text may be sent to the search engine to run the search. Apple also notes that cellular data charges may apply.


## How to dictate text on iPhone


Once Dictation is on, the steps are the same in every app:


1. Tap in a text field to place the cursor where you want the words to go.
2. Tap the **microphone** key on the onscreen keyboard (it also appears inside some text fields).
3. When the microphone icon shows near the cursor, start talking.
4. To stop, tap the microphone again, say **"Stop dictation"** , or simply stop talking: Dictation turns itself off after 30 seconds of silence.


The keyboard stays open while you dictate, so you can type a word, say a sentence, and type again without switching modes. That is the habit that makes iPhone voice to text feel natural: talk the bulk of the message, then tap to fix the one word it missed.


If you dictate in more than one language, add a keyboard for each one. Apple says that when you use a keyboard for another language, Dictation works in that language too, so switching keyboards with the globe key also switches the language you are dictating in.


## Voice commands for punctuation, formatting, and editing


In supported languages, Dictation now adds commas, periods, and question marks on its own as you speak. You can still say punctuation out loud when you want control. The commands Apple lists include:


Say


You get


"period", "comma", "question mark", "exclamation point"


. , ? !


"colon", "semicolon", "dollar sign", "hashtag"


: ; $ #


"open parenthesis" / "close parenthesis"


( )


"quote" / "end quote"


quotation marks


"new line" / "new paragraph"


a line break or a new paragraph


"cap"


capitalizes the next word


"all caps"


makes the next word uppercase


"caps on" ... "caps off"


capitalizes each word in between


"no space on" ... "no space off"


runs the words together (not in every language)


"heart emoji", "smiley emoji"


the emoji, in supported languages


Dictation also understands a handful of editing commands:


- **"Change \[text\] to \[text\]"** replaces a word or phrase, for example "Change tea to T-E-E."
- **"Insert \[text\] before \[text\]"** and **"Insert \[text\] after \[text\]"** add words in place.
- **"Select \[text\]"** and **"Delete \[text\]"** act on a phrase you name, and **"Delete all"** clears the field.
- **"Undo"** and **"Redo"** reverse or repeat the last command.
- To spell a name, say it and then spell it: "Let's invite Steven S-T-E-P-H-E-N."


One limit matters here: Apple says the editing commands (change, insert, select, delete) work in U.S. English on iPhone 12 and later, except iPhone SE. Punctuation and formatting commands work more widely. If automatic punctuation gets in the way, turn it off under **Settings > General > Keyboard > Auto-Punctuation** .


What is new in iOS 27: with Apple Intelligence, Dictation uses an on-device model to improve spelling, punctuation, and capitalization. Apple limits that to English on iPhone 17 Pro, iPhone 17 Pro Max, iPhone Air, or later, so most iPhones in use today get the standard Dictation described above.


## iPhone dictation not working? Try these fixes


Most "voice to text stopped working" problems come down to a handful of causes. Work through them in order.


### The microphone key is missing


Go back to **Settings > General > Keyboard** and check that **Enable Dictation** is on. If it is already on, turning it off and on again is a quick first fix. Also check which keyboard is showing: the Dictation microphone belongs to Apple's keyboard, so if you have switched to a third-party keyboard, tap or hold the globe key to switch back (or use that keyboard's own voice feature).


### It types the wrong language


Dictation follows the keyboard you have selected. If you have more than one keyboard installed, the globe key decides which language Dictation listens for. Add or remove keyboards under **Settings > General > Keyboard > Keyboards** . Apple also notes that Dictation is not available in every language, country, or region, and features vary.


### It stops on its own


That is by design. Dictation turns off after 30 seconds of silence. If you pause to think, tap the microphone again to resume where the cursor is.


### "Change" and "Delete" do nothing


The editing commands need U.S. English on an iPhone 12 or later (not iPhone SE). On other languages or older phones, Dictation will type the words "change" and "delete" instead of acting on them. Edit by hand, or use a tool with its own voice editing (below).


### It mishears everything


Check the basics: take off a case or screen cover that might block the microphones, make sure nothing is connected that could be taking the microphone input (a Bluetooth headset you forgot about is a common one), and test the microphone by recording a short clip in the Voice Memos app. If the recording sounds muffled, the problem is the microphone, not Dictation. Speak at a normal pace in full phrases; Dictation uses the surrounding words to pick the right ones.


### It still does not work


Restart the iPhone, then install any pending iOS update under **Settings > General > Software Update** . If the phone is managed by a school or employer, or has Screen Time restrictions set by a parent, a restriction may be blocking Dictation; ask whoever manages the device. If none of that helps, contact Apple Support, since the microphone itself may need service.


## Where built-in iPhone dictation falls short


Apple's Dictation is free, private, and good enough for texts and quick notes. Where it runs out is longer, real writing on the phone:


- **Your words.** Apple does not document a way to teach Dictation your vocabulary, so names, product terms, and jargon come out wrong the same way every time.
- **Editing.** Voice editing is limited to swapping, inserting, and deleting exact phrases, only in U.S. English on newer iPhones. You cannot say "make this shorter" or "turn this into a list."
- **Cleanup.** Dictation types what you say, including the "um, actually, wait" parts. Turning a spoken ramble into a message you would send is still a job for your thumbs.
- **The newest model is gated.** The Apple Intelligence improvements are English-only and limited to the latest iPhones.


If those do not bother you, stay with Dictation. If they do, that is the gap a dedicated app fills.

## Voice to text on your other devices


The same habits carry over. On a Mac, Dictation works much the same way, with a keyboard shortcut; see[how to use dictation on Mac](https://aquavoice.com/blog/how-to-use-dictation-on-mac) , and[Mac dictation not working](https://aquavoice.com/blog/mac-dictation-not-working) if it stops. On Android,[talk to text with Gboard](https://aquavoice.com/blog/talk-to-text-android) is the built-in equivalent.


## FAQ


### How do I turn on voice to text on my iPhone?


Open Settings, tap General, then Keyboard, and turn on Enable Dictation. A microphone key then appears on the keyboard in any app. Tap it, speak, and tap it again (or say "Stop dictation") when you are done.


### Why is there no microphone on my iPhone keyboard?


Usually Dictation is turned off, or you are using a third-party keyboard. Turn on Enable Dictation under Settings > General > Keyboard, then use the globe key to switch back to Apple's keyboard. Dictation is also not available in every language or region.


### Does iPhone voice to text work without internet?


In many languages, yes. Apple says Dictation is processed on the iPhone and needs no internet connection in those languages. Text you dictate into a search field may still be sent to the search engine.


### Can I edit text by voice on iPhone?


Partly. Built-in Dictation understands "change ... to ...", "insert ... before ...", "select", "delete", "undo", and "redo", in U.S. English on iPhone 12 and later (not iPhone SE). For rewrites in plain language, such as "make this shorter", you need an app like Aqua Voice with voice editing.
